title: Cap your hardest thinking at four to five hours per day.
subtitle: Cognitive load ceiling
rationale: Beyond the cap, fatigue degrades judgment on hard problems; stop the hard work and switch to lighter tasks.

evidence.summary: Elite-performer practice records cluster around 4-5 focused hours daily; direct trials on knowledge work are lacking.

sources.label: Paul Graham, How to Do Great Work

indications: Evening work on hard problems produces code or writing that gets reverted.
Deep-work hours are treated as unlimited.
